home.title: Welcome to TradeRock
home.intro: TradeRock pretends to be a second Switch in the FireRed and LeafGreen trade room. That way you send Pokémon from your PC to your game and keep the ones you receive.

settings.engineHelp: The engine is what talks to the Switch. The Wi-Fi card becomes available once set up in the wizard; the ESP32 comes in a later version.
settings.maxAttemptsHelp: How many times TradeRock tries to connect before giving up. Connecting to the Switch sometimes takes a few attempts.
settings.phaseTimeoutSeconds: Maximum idle time inside the room (seconds)
settings.nationalDex: My save already has the National Pokédex
settings.choosePokemon: Pick a Pokémon you caught on the Switch
settings.allowIllegalHelp: Off: TradeRock won't send the Switch a Pokémon PKHeX considers illegal. On: each trade with an illegal one still asks for confirmation.

blockers.species_unobtainable: Species: no way to obtain it in Gen 3 games.

inject.intro: Puts vault Pokémon into the boxes of a FireRed, LeafGreen, Ruby, Sapphire or Emerald save. Before writing, TradeRock keeps a copy of the original save.

inject.downloadMode: After injecting, download the new save and replace the file in your emulator.

preview.wifi_compatible: Your PC has the {{model}} card, which is compatible. You may not need to buy anything!

preview.vm: You're in a virtual machine ({{vm}}): the Wi-Fi card isn't reachable. Use an ESP32 or real Linux.

wizard.keysOk: Valid format. Supported protocols: {{protocols}}. Final confirmation comes in the Switch test.

reasons.windows: Windows doesn't allow the Wi-Fi access trading needs.

wizard.usbAdapterTitle: Alternative: a compatible USB Wi-Fi adapter
wizard.usbAdapterPros: Pros: same path as the Wi-Fi card and keeps your internet free. Cons: costs more than an ESP32 and only works on Linux.
wizard.esp32Pros: ESP32: cheaper, works on Linux and Windows, doesn't touch your network. Cons: needs firmware flashed (TradeRock does it).
wizard.choosePort: Which port is the ESP32 on?
wizard.noPorts: No port found. Plug the ESP32 in with a data cable.
wizard.confirmModule: Checked: the module metal shield says ESP32-WROOM-32E.
wizard.moduleHelp: Read the name printed on the module metal shield (the silver part with the antenna).
wizard.availableIn: Coming in a later version of the app ({{what}}).
wizard.blockedTrade: Real trading unlocks once every essential item is OK. Demo mode stays available.
wizard.notReady: Something is still missing for real trading.
wizard.banner: Set up TradeRock to trade with your Switch.

checks.keys_skipped: prod.keys skipped: real trading stays locked.
checks.radio_unavailable: The chosen radio isn't available on this PC.
checks.not_native_windows: The Wi-Fi card only works on Linux.
checks.not_native_wsl: WSL doesn't reach the Wi-Fi card: use real Linux or an ESP32.
checks.not_native_vm: Virtual machines don't reach the Wi-Fi card: use real Linux or an ESP32.
checks.phy_untested: {{driver}} card: untested; the card test will tell.
checks.phy_is_internet: This card is the PC's internet ({{iface}}): internet drops while trading. Use a network cable or a second adapter.
checks.esp32_board_not_chosen: Tell us which ESP32 you have.
checks.esp32_confirm_module: Check that the module is ESP32-WROOM-32E.
checks.esp32_board_untested: {{model}}: no complete trade reported with this firmware.
checks.serial_none: No serial port found: plug the ESP32 in with a data cable.
checks.usb_driver_missing: The {{chip}} converter driver is missing. Install it from the manufacturer official page.
checks.port_should_be_native: The {{model}} uses native USB, but this port is a USB-serial converter. Check the board port.
checks.port_should_be_uart: The {{model}} uses the USB-serial converter, but this port is native USB. Use the other port.
checks.serial_group_missing: Your user isn't in the {{group}} group (serial port access).
checks.serial_group_relogin: You joined the {{group}} group: log out and back in for it to take effect.
checks.brltty_running: brltty is running and often "hijacks" CH340/CP210x converters. If you don’t use a braille display, disable it.
checks.udev_rule_optional: Optional: udev rule so the port is always named {{path}}.
checks.esp32_firmware_pending: Check and flash the ESP32 firmware.
checks.worker_missing: Network component not installed. It ships with the TradeRock package (.deb); if you built the app yourself, run scripts/dev-host.sh.
checks.pkexec_missing: pkexec is missing (the system uses it to ask for the administrator password).
checks.worker_unsafe: The network component install ({{path}}) can be changed without administrator rights. For safety, TradeRock won't use it. Reinstall it.
checks.worker_policy_missing: The network component permission (polkit policy) is not installed. Reinstall TradeRock.
checks.worker_installed: Network component installed. The administrator password is asked once, when it's first used.
checks.tools_missing: Programs the engine uses to control the card are missing: {{tools}}.
checks.card_test_not_run: Test the {{model}} card ({{phy}}) below: this test tells whether it works.
checks.card_test_passed: The {{model}} card ({{phy}}) passed: it entered monitor mode and transmitted.
checks.card_test_failed: The {{model}} card ({{phy}}) failed the test. See the result below.
checks.card_test_passed_no_rx: The card transmitted but received nothing during the test. It may just be that there are no Wi-Fi networks nearby; if trading can't find the Switch, suspect reception.
checks.card_test_passed_some_channels: The card works but didn't tune to every channel (1, 6 and 11). Trading may fail if the Switch uses one of them.
checks.network_manager_ok: NetworkManager set up so it doesn't interfere with trading.
checks.network_manager_unconfigured: NetworkManager may interfere with trading. Set it up below (recommended).

deliveries.entrega-7: Switch test with the Wi-Fi card

cardTest.title: Card test ({{phy}})
cardTest.help: The test puts the card in monitor mode and transmits the frames the Switch's room uses. It takes about 10 seconds and needs neither the Switch nor prod.keys.
cardTest.password: The first time, the system asks for the administrator password (the system asks, not TradeRock). It then stays valid until you close the app.
cardTest.offline: During the test, this card's normal Wi-Fi is turned off. It comes back by itself at the end.
cardTest.offlineInternet: Heads up: this card is the PC's internet. During the test (and during trades) the internet drops and comes back by itself at the end.
cardTest.needsWorker: First sort out the network component (see the list below).
cardTest.needsTools: First install the missing programs (see the list below).
cardTest.waitPassword: If the system password window shows up, type the administrator password.

codes.passed: The card passed: monitor mode and transmission work.
codes.passed_no_rx: The card transmitted but received no frames.
codes.passed_some_channels: The card passed but didn't tune to every channel.
codes.monitor_failed: The card refused monitor mode. Its driver doesn't work for LDN.
codes.channel_failed: The card entered monitor mode but couldn't tune to any channel. Another program may be using it.
codes.tx_failed: The card couldn't transmit in monitor mode. Its driver doesn't work for LDN.
codes.card_test_crashed: The test stopped with an error. Try again; if it keeps happening, export the report from the summary.

cardTest.optionsMany: You can test again, pick another card in the list above, or use an ESP32 instead of the Wi-Fi card.
cardTest.optionsOne: You can test again or use an ESP32 instead of the Wi-Fi card.

network.title: NetworkManager
network.help: For each trade, the engine creates a temporary wireless connection (named starting with "ldn"). If NetworkManager tries to manage it, the trade authenticates but never completes. This setting tells it to ignore those connections; your internet is unchanged.
network.confirmText: TradeRock will create these two files (as administrator) and reload the NetworkManager configuration, without dropping your current connection:
